0.comment: Zhongli: Guizhong and the Guili Assembly
0.content:
Before Liyue Harbor existed, Morax and Guizhong, the God of Dust, built a settlement of humans and adepti on the Guili Plains, named after them both; the gods there included Marchosius, the God of the Stove. In the Archon War a catastrophic battle laid waste to the Guili Plains and Dihua Marsh, and Guizhong perished. Morax led the survivors south of Mt. Tianheng and founded Liyue Harbor with the adepti about 3,700 years ago. The Guizhong Ballista on Mt. Tianheng and Guizhong's collected treasures preserve her legacy. Zhongli rarely speaks of her directly.

Glaze Lilies, which he sent the Traveler to gather for the Rite of Parting, are tied to that age; his birthday gift is a dried Glaze Lily said to bloom "bearing the weight of the beautiful memories and prayers of the land". Marchosius later spent his power protecting Liyue and dwindled into the little creature Xiangling calls Guoba.

1.comment: Zhongli: The Rite of Descension and the Rite of Parting
1.content:
Every year Rex Lapis descended to give Liyue its oracle for the year. At the last Rite of Descension (1.0) his body fell from the sky, apparently assassinated, and the Qixing locked down the harbor; the Traveler was suspected and fled with Childe's help. Childe introduced them to Zhongli, who said it was his duty to give Rex Lapis a proper farewell. Spending Fatui Mora freely, Zhongli and the Traveler gathered Noctilucous Jade, Silk Flower perfumes, the Cleansing Bell from Madame Ping and Glaze Lilies. The body was an "exuvia", a shed form, stored at the Golden House.

After Childe released Osial and Liyue's people, Qixing and adepti defeated it without their god, Zhongli met Signora and Childe at the Northland Bank and revealed everything. He had feigned his death and "gathered the cast of Childe, the adepti, and the Liyue Qixing to play their roles together on the stage that was Liyue." The adepti showed restraint and cooperation, and the Qixing seized control, which he called the best possible outcome. He had already told the Qixing, through Ningguang, that he lived, and left the official story to them. At the Rite of Parting they announced that Rex Lapis's soul had returned to the heavens after a divine trial, and he watched, relaxed, "after laying down the burden I have borne for 3,700 years."

2.comment: Zhongli: The Contract to End All Contracts
2.content:
Zhongli's last contract as Geo Archon was with the Cryo Archon: he would hand over the Geo Gnosis, which Signora collected peacefully after the Rite of Parting. He had kept it in reserve in case his test failed and Liyue fell into chaos. Even mortals contract on "equivalent exchange", yet what the Tsaritsa wagered to balance the scales has never been revealed. He says no trade is truly worth a Gnosis, and that a clause forbids him to divulge the contract's contents.

He credited Signora with keeping his secret "despite the eavesdropping ears of her colleague, Childe". Without the Gnosis, Mora can no longer be minted, and the Golden House has stayed closed. The Fatui were last confirmed to hold six Gnoses; the Pyro Gnosis has been unaccounted for since the Nod-Krai events. Zhongli has said nothing on-screen about her goals.

3.content:
Long ago an evil god learned a young yaksha's weakness and forced him to commit atrocities and devour dreams. Morax freed him and gave him the name Xiao to protect him. Xiao, as Alatus, became one of the five foremost yakshas, who fought the lingering hatred of buried gods; he is the last still fighting, burdened by karmic debt. Zhongli sighs that he is "still fulfilling his duty to this very day" and sends him medicine, warning that Paimon must not eat it. Xiao reveres Rex Lapis absolutely and is puzzled by Zhongli's mortal hobbies ("Birds, antiques, flowers... What deeper meaning do they hold?").

In the Chasm (2.7) Xiao saved everyone else from collapsing tunnels and was about to be lost when Zhongli intervened at the final moment. In 6.3 Xiao gathered the adepti on Rex Lapis's orders and trusted that his lord had entrusted the matter to the Traveler for a reason. In 7.1, Xiao is stationed at The Chasm because "Rex Lapis tasked me with monitoring this place."

4.content:
When Barbatos first came to Liyue, Rex Lapis prepared to help a neighbour in crisis, and Barbatos tossed him a wine bottle: "Here's some wine from Mondstadt. Care for a taste?" He kept visiting with endless questions, and the first Seven began to gather in Liyue. Of that first table, only the two of them still hold their seats. Zhongli can smell when the bard has been nearby ("It reeks of wine"), calls him a drunkard and a disgrace to the arts, and offers to brew sobering tea that takes six hours. He says a friend from Mondstadt always brought Dandelion Wine.

Venti practised forging Morax's seal as a prank and never fooled him, and calls him an "old block-head". At Liyue's Lantern Rite (3.4, limited event) the two recognised each other and agreed to pretend they had not. Despite the bickering, Zhongli's reminiscences about "those who share the memory" are largely about that circle.

5.content:
Azhdaha was a blind Geo dragon from beneath Liyue. Morax answered his wish, brought him above ground, gave him sight and made a contract: he could live among people, but if he ever brought ruin to order he would be sealed in the dark again. Erosion ground away Azhdaha's memories, and mining that shook the Ley Lines drove him mad with pain. A thousand years ago he attacked The Chasm; Morax fought him through the mines and sealed him beneath an ancient tree at Nantianmen. The Dragonfall stone was born in that battle.

In No Mere Stone (1.5) the seal loosened. Azhdaha's power took the form of a child who lured miners to dig toward it, while his benevolent half possessed the artisan Kun Jun to find Morax. With Kun Jun's help, Zhongli and the Traveler subdued and resealed the dragon. Zhongli told Azhdaha, speaking through Kun Jun, "I am no longer the Geo Archon," and he answered that he could sense it. Asked whether he hesitated that day in The Chasm: "A heart of stone is a heart nonetheless." Zhongli called sealing an old friend "just one form of erosion I have endured".

key: Have I already finished my duties
6.content: Erosion is the wearing-away of memory and self that long-lived beings suffer; Kun Jun called it "the world's greatest destroyer of memories". Zhongli admits he is not immune: "Even boulders that can withstand whirlpools will erode with the passing of time." He kept telling himself no cracks had formed until a merchant's casual words, "You've finished your duties, go ahead and call it a day", made him ask whether his own were done. He sees stepping down as understanding "When the door opens, it is time to leave," and wonders whether giving up what one loves to follow the right path is the erosion the Heavenly Principles imposed on him.

7.comment: Zhongli: Ganyu, Ningguang, Keqing and the Qixing
7.content: Ganyu is the servant who has honoured her contract longest; Zhongli will not tell her story for her, fearing his wording "would not be delicate enough". She has absolute faith in Rex Lapis and remembers centuries of camaraderie. Ningguang he admires as "a rare gem", recalling her walking barefoot from Yaoguang Shoal to sell her wares. Through her he secretly told the Qixing that he lived. Ningguang, for her part, finds him a useful man whose weaknesses she does not yet know. Keqing is "the most impious of the Qixing"; people like her, who speak up and act decisively, made his retirement possible. She respects Zhongli but finds him as traditional as Rex Lapis. The Qixing's seizure of power after his "death" delighted him.

8.comment: Zhongli: Hu Tao and Wangsheng Funeral Parlor
8.content: Wangsheng's Hu family has handled funerals for 77 generations. Director Hu Tao focuses on mortals, so for the rare rites of "sending off" adepti she employs Zhongli, whose ceremonies no scholar can fault. Locals call him "living history"; he only smiles and says he has a good memory. He "cannot deal with that child", yet goes along on her errands and expenses; he charges purchases to Wangsheng. Hu Tao thinks he looks young but has a "dusty" personality and half-suspects what he is. During a limited 5.3 Lantern Rite event he watched her rite against the fetor, then explained her name to Mountain Shaper.

9.content: Childe was sent to Liyue for the Gnosis without being told of the contract. He introduced the Traveler to Zhongli and funded the Rite of Parting. When the Gnosis was not in the Exuvia, he used replicated Sigils of Permission to free the sealed god Osial and force Rex Lapis out; the people of Liyue stopped it instead. At the Northland Bank Childe complained that Signora and Zhongli had deceived him. Zhongli calls him "that rascal from Snezhnaya", offers to "deal with the matter swiftly" if he makes trouble, and looks forward to drinks and Fatui gossip with him. Childe wants a duel to settle the "fiasco".

10.comment: Zhongli: Zibai, the White Horse Adeptus
10.content:
Zibai was an envoy of the Three Moons who ruled Lang-Gan and befriended Morax in a remote age; she first saw him fighting as three identical selves under the battle cry "The Lord of Geo, Heaven's Star!", and he taught her to excise the Three Deadly Selves. When divine punishment fell on her nation she severed her Selves and died, and the avatar of Time preserved her soul's fragments within them. In the 6.3 Lantern Rite story quest A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon (first released with a time-limited event, now a permanent Story Quest), Zhongli explained that the shadowmoon, her prison, was disintegrating now that a new moon had been born, and that the Traveler had brought the Frost Moon back. He asked the Traveler to help reunite her Heavenly, Earthly and Human souls before the festival night.

Zhongli tracked down Ziqiao, the free-spirited Third Self who had fought for him in the Archon War after he freed her from a painting. He offered her a contract: a one-day tour of modern Liyue Harbor, with the Traveler and Paimon as guides. Moved by the ordinary life she saw, Ziqiao gave up the Human Soul and faded. Zhongli watched from a distance; asked if he was just bad at goodbyes, he fell silent. At the Rite he and the Traveler released the soul fragments in a Xiao Lantern ("Devoted soul, scattered and unbound, let this lantern guide you home"). Zibai descended onto Yujing Terrace, and he greeted her: "Zibai, my friend, welcome home."

Before this, Zhongli had found the Earthly Self's trace on a jade carriage excavated from The Chasm at a Xigu Antiques exhibition. He sent a Geo pillar to the adepti that only the Traveler could read, and told the adepti to wait rather than act against Zizhi. Ganyu relayed Cloud Retainer's realisation that the old Moonchase Rite he performed may have been an attempt to reach Zibai. His voice-over calls her "an old acquaintance... one I haven't met in a very long time." Zibai notes she was not named White Horse Adeptus by Morax.

11.content: The adepti signed a contract with Rex Lapis to protect Liyue 3,700 years ago. Madame Ping, who held the Cleansing Bell an "old friend" gave her, realised he had stepped down before he told the others. After the Osial crisis the adepti retired further and accepted the Qixing's leadership. Cloud Retainer now lives in the harbor as Xianyun. Zhongli vouched for her goods to the merchant Shaozu, insisted on calling her Xianyun "as a friend should", and reminded her she had once missed his Bamboo Shoot Soup. Shenhe's master told her to let him sit quietly if he drinks before her abode. Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver still gather at Mt. Aocang when he calls.

12.content: Ei: he feasted with her when she was Makoto's kagemusha. "Time tempers all volition. Yet she would give up everyone for her beliefs." He would like to learn of her Eternity; she says his story is far from finished. In 1.1 he warned that his "death" would harden her resolve behind the Vision Hunt Decree. Nahida (Buer): "All life in Teyvat owes her gratitude for saving Irminsul." Furina: her five-century contract with herself, which "even fooled the Heavenly Principles", earns his great respect. Mavuika (Haborym): a leader with "strength that rivals the gods". Neuvillette says "Deus Auri" must one day be called to trial; Zhongli quietly avoided him at Qiaoying (4.4, limited event).

13.comment: Zhongli: Liyue's Titles for Rex Lapis
13.content: Liyue gives its god many titles: God of Contracts for its laws, God of Commerce for the first Mora, God of History as eldest of The Seven, God of the Stove for the gift of fire and hearth, and Warrior God, the opera hero beloved by children. Many Liyue tales are stories of people their god once visited in disguise: dishes he discovered while lost, plaques in his handwriting, an opera in which he played a warrior. The Rex Incognito books exaggerate his shapeshifting, and the Stove God's legends in fact belonged to Marchosius before merging into his.

14.content: After the Azhdaha battle the Traveler asked Zhongli about Khaenri'ah and their sibling, recalling what Dainsleif told them. He answered, "I cannot say." He had signed a contract "before it all began" and has kept his silence ever since. He said it brings him no pleasure to disappoint his friends, but the God of Contracts cannot go back on his word. Instead he told them the truth has been eroded and forgotten, but they can bring it to light: "Those who come to witness... will witness. Those who are born to remember... will remember."
